thread.title: UPDATE: AMD's stock soars higher but Micron tumbles as chip makers continue to slide

author: morningstar.com
title: UPDATE: AMD's stock soars higher but Micron tumbles as chip makers continue to slide
text:
By Wallace Witkowski, MarketWatch
Micron leads S&P 500 decliners, but AMD up 18% on week
Chip stocks were hammered for a second day Wednesday as more analysts accepted that memory-chip demand for the remainder of the year will not be as strong as expected as recently as a few months ago. And for a second straight day, shares of Advanced Micro Devices Inc. powered higher.
On Wednesday, Goldman Sachs analysts downgraded Micron Inc. (MU) and Lam Research Corp. (LRCX) because of weaker-than-expected demand for memory chips (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-leads-memory-stocks-lower-after-goldman-downgrades-on-fear-of-downturn-2018-09-12). Micron shares, which were Wednesday's worst performer on the S&P 500 index closed down 4.3% at $41.74, and are up a scant 1.5% for the year. Lam shares finished down 3.2%.
Meanwhile, the PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 1.2%, while the S&P 500 rose less than 0.1% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index declined 0.2%. The SOX index, which had been up as much as 15% on the year, is now up 7.4% year to date, compared with an 8.1% gain in the S&P 500 and a 15.2% gain in the Nasdaq.
On Tuesday, RBC analyst Amit Daryanani lowered his price target on Micron (Amit%20Daryanani%20lowered%20his%20price%20target%20on%20the%20stock) to $70 from $83, citing memory-chip weakness.
All year, the debate has raged: Are memory chips heading for a delayed downturn given the supply-and-demand cycle inherent in the industry, or has the nature of the cycle been changed and we're now in uncharted territory because high demand for data centers and cloud applications has disrupted normal cycles?
As that debate has played out, the SOX chip index has staggered above and below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages. With Wednesday's round of downgrades, the SOX index once again fell below its 200-day moving average for the fourth time since April.
The types of chips in question are DRAM, or dynamic random access memory, the type of memory commonly used in PCs and servers, and NAND, the flash memory chips that are used in USB drives and smaller devices such as digital cameras.
Back in April, analysts were predicting soft demand for memory chips (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-nvidia-weigh-as-chip-makers-hamper-tech-gains-2018-04-05), saying that Micron could be stretched thin in the buying cycle, and by the end of that month even Apple Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/micron-stock-dips-after-apple-cfo-predicts-memory-prices-will-turn-around-this-year-2018-05-01).(AAPL) was predicting a fall in memory prices. Then, Micron shares hit their highest price since the dot-com bust (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/microns-stock-trades-at-highest-level-since-dot-com-bust-2018-05-29)in late May after the company raised its outlook and announced a $10 billion share buyback. That optimism all started falling apart when Micron itself and KLA-Tencor Inc. (KLAC) said last week that demand was not as strong as had been expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chip-related-stocks-look-at-worst-day-in-nearly-two-months-on-forecast-weakness-2018-09-06).
One of the few chip stocks posting gains Wednesday was AMD (AMD) , which added to gains in an unprecedented run over the past 97 trading days. AMD shares closed up 7% at $32.21, their highest close since May 22, 2006 when they finished at $33.18, according to FactSet data. Shares are up nearly 18% this week alone.
After closing at a 52-week low of $9.53 on April 9, AMD shares have skyrocketed more than 220% since then. Shares closed above $30 for the first time in more than 12 years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amd-price-hike-not-enough-to-overcome-chip-stock-slip-as-memory-chip-woes-settle-in-2018-09-11) after Rosenblatt Securities analyst Hans Mosesmann hiked his price target on AMD to $40 from $30, making him once again Wall Street's most bullish analyst on the stock.
Read:AMD short sellers gutted by 'stealthy short squeeze' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/amd-short-sellers-gutted-by-stealthy-short-squeeze-2018-08-27)
Other chip stocks underperforming the SOX index on Wednesday were Analog Devices Inc. (ADI) , Applied Materials Inc. (AMAT) , Entegris Inc. (ENTG) , KLA-Tencor, Marvell Technology Group Ltd. (MRVL) , Maxim Integrated Products Inc. (MXIM) , Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) , Skyworks Solutions Inc. (SWKS) , Teradyne Inc. (TER) and Texas Instruments Inc. (TXN) .
-Wallace Witkowski; 1716ET
